observations.text: Round 3 scope and selection, re-recorded on clean HEAD ce16980. The reviewed scope is clean at this commit: git diff --stat ce16980 is empty, so the working tree equals the commit, and the only untracked paths are my own draft directory and the crafter run record, both outside the reviewed scope. Read the rebuilt bundle oracle-review.S1.r2.prompt (1395 lines) and diffed it against the superseded one: TASK, RECORD, ROLE VERBS and worked examples unchanged; the support set gains crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_canzan_theme.rs, partials/sidebar.html becomes an Extend target for exactly one id, the stylesheet is cited by its landed name foundry.4c73f62c.css, and the impact row for the theme step file is now Changed with the reason REFUTED BY A REAL RUN rather than predicted. Mechanical selection of the oracle and support delta since my last approval: git diff ff737aa 0529072 --stat lists five paths of which exactly one is a test file, feature_canzan_theme.rs with 25 lines touched, the other four being design records and my own published review record; that file is byte-identical to /Users/jeffbailey/.cache/nwdes/nav-collapse-toggle/oracle.S1.r2.diff, two hunks, the neighbour-arm docstring and the arm itself. The production commit ce16980 touched no file of the acceptance crate: git diff --stat 0529072 ce16980 -- crates/foundry-acceptance is empty, and so is the diff over the other four oracle and support paths since ff737aa, so the oracle approved in rounds one and two is unchanged and only this delta is reassessed.

Evidence for the delta, reused on clean HEAD ce16980 with the comparison that justifies it; no new execution and nothing restamped. Original run, cited as its own: host execution on the tree now committed, timeout 2700 scripts/test-in-lima.sh bash -c "cargo fmt -p foundry-acceptance -- --check; ...; env FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=us-cts-04 CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=4 cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --release", log /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-canzan-foundry/ae6f0864-8ca5-43d5-b970-fb78c37ae831/scratchpad/theme_arm.log, FMT_EXIT=0, summary "9 scenarios (9 passed), 68 steps (68 passed)". The restated step is neither skipped nor vacuous by absence: the log shows the scenario "A chosen dark screen never flashes light" with all seven of its steps green, including "Then the theme is settled before the browser is permitted to paint", the step that carries the arm. Unchanged-input comparison at this commit: the oracle revision the run read is 0529072, whose acceptance-crate bytes ce16980 does not touch; the production bytes the run read are the bytes ce16980 records, since git diff --stat ce16980 is empty and committing did not rewrite them, their mtimes still being 2026-11-16T23:26:10 to 23:48:12 against a log mtime of 2026-11-17T00:22:33, and the theme step file itself 00:05:10; the runtime is the same local-dev VM and the same release profile. No relevant input changed, so no affected check needs repeating and I launched no rerun. Independent arithmetic at ce16980 confirming the refutation the restatement answers: git show ce16980:crates/foundry-app/templates/base.html declares ten head script tags, nine with src, two of them non-deferring (theme.js at line 48, nav-collapse.js at line 65) and seven carrying defer, so the old arm computed deferred_neighbours 7 against the required head_scripts.len() minus 1 equal to 8 and failed with "1 of the 8", which is the reported us-cts-04 exit 101, while the restated arm holds with a margin of 7.

Judgment of the restated arm, re-recorded on clean HEAD ce16980: the anti-vacuity purpose is kept intact and the theme promise loses nothing it needs. The arm exists so that arm (a), theme.js carries none of defer, async or type=module, cannot hold for the wrong reason on a head where NOTHING defers and the parse therefore cannot tell the two shapes apart. assert!(deferred_neighbours > 0) fails on exactly that condition and on no other, so the guard is preserved rather than softened, and its own failure message states that precise reason. What the restatement drops is a different and stronger claim, that theme.js is the ONLY non-deferring head script. The theme promise does not rest on it: a second render-blocking head script cannot push theme.js past first paint, because a render-blocking tag delays the paint it precedes, so no arrangement of additional pre-paint scripts can reintroduce the flash of the light palette. That claim is also now false by authorized design, which adds a second pre-paint script, so keeping the count would make a shipped lane fail against a design change rather than against a defect, which the us-cts-04 exit 101 already demonstrated. The law the count was gesturing at, that every script which must run before first paint is render-blocking and that a third one added later is still refused, is a law over a growing set and is carried by the architectural obligation T1 in xtask/src/check_arch.rs run by cargo xtask check-arch, which the design names as its proper owner and which a scenario about one tag cannot express. Nothing else is weakened: the two hunks touch only the docstring paragraph and the arm, arms (a) and (b) and the recorded-choice assertion are untouched, so a defer added to theme.js still fails deterministically and a head where every neighbour stops deferring still fails the restated arm. The shape is now identical to the neighbour arm the nav lane carries at feature_nav_collapse.rs:1951, so the two lanes express one guard instead of two divergent versions of it. Residual, recorded and not demanded: no acceptance scenario now asserts the exact membership of the non-deferring head set, which is T1 territory; I do not invent a scenario for it.

Retained judgments, expected polarity and limits, re-recorded on clean HEAD ce16980. GREEN is the correct observed result for this delta and no RED is demanded of it: the arm pins behaviour that already ships, the theme promise is already built, and a test that pins existing behaviour needs only to pass. The nav-collapse oracle own semantic RED stands as recorded in the earlier rounds and is not re-observed here, nor is it re-claimed against the now-implemented production: the reused 32-case run with 0 parsing and 0 hook errors, plus the degraded-lane execution at 53ffb7f with exit 101, one already-satisfied P5 pass and two semantic RED. Everything outside this delta is retained unexamined: both-direction closure over P1-P6 and L1-L7, L8 in the T1 gate, the authority-backed limits on first-frame pixels, the unreachable storage-refused press on a signed-in screen and the JS-runner deviation for the broad half of L5, and the two round-one findings that round two closed by design amendment. This review did not and does not judge the production in ce16980, which is the crafter artifact and another role scope; it is cited only as the unchanged input the reused run read. Minor and not a finding: the docstring of arm (a) still recalls DISCUSS naming "the five neighbouring tags" as the likely regression, which is a true record of a past decision rather than a live claim, and no assertion depends on it. typesafe: unavailable still holds, with no call re-attempted this round, so every judgment here is reviewer_reason from local evidence, namely the two diff hunks, the served shell head arithmetic at ce16980, the host log and the comparison above.

diagnostic: ACCEPTED. Re-approval of the round-3 oracle delta only, on clean HEAD ce16980: one test file, crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_canzan_theme.rs, two hunks, the neighbour-arm docstring and the arm itself. The restatement from assert_eq!(deferred_neighbours, head_scripts.len() - 1) to assert!(deferred_neighbours > 0) keeps the arm anti-vacuity purpose exactly: it fails on precisely the condition that would let arm (a) hold for the wrong reason, a head where nothing defers and the parse cannot tell a render-blocking tag from a deferred one, and at this commit it holds with a margin of seven deferring neighbours out of eight. It weakens nothing the theme promise needs. The dropped claim, that theme.js is the ONLY non-deferring head script, was never load-bearing for no flash of the light palette, because a render-blocking tag delays the paint it precedes and so no additional pre-paint script can push theme.js past first paint; that claim is now false by authorized design, which is why the shipped lane exited 101 against a design change rather than against a defect. The law over the growing set of pre-paint scripts is carried by the architectural obligation T1 in xtask/src/check_arch.rs, which the design names as its proper owner, so no obligation is left unowned. Arms (a) and (b) and the recorded-choice assertion are untouched, so a defer on theme.js still fails deterministically and a head where every neighbour stops deferring still fails the restated arm; the arm is now the same shape as the nav lane own neighbour guard at feature_nav_collapse.rs:1951, so the two lanes express one guard rather than two divergent ones. Evidence reused with its comparison, not restamped: the host us-cts-04 run with FMT_EXIT=0 and 9 scenarios, 68 steps all passed, the restated step itself green inside the scenario "A chosen dark screen never flashes light"; its oracle revision 0529072 is untouched by ce16980, whose production bytes are the bytes that run read, git diff --stat ce16980 being empty and every input mtime predating the log; so no affected check needed repeating and no rerun was launched. GREEN is the right polarity here: the arm pins shipped behaviour, while the nav-collapse semantic RED of the earlier rounds stands as recorded and is not re-claimed against the now-implemented production. The rest of the oracle is unchanged and every judgment outside this delta is retained. No finding, so no owner is contacted. The production in ce16980 is another role artifact and is not judged here. typesafe: unavailable; reviewer_reason throughout. Completion obligations unchanged: implementation GREEN for all 32 nav-collapse cases, and close evidence naming the lane that actually ran, since a gate without Docker observes none of them.
